claims.quote: and  of  the  injury  that  will  be  inflicted  by  the  new weapons.
claims.description: New small-calibre rifle bullets will cause far more deaths and suffering in the next war than earlier weapons did.

claims.quote: Probably  with  attempts  on  outposts  made  by  sharpshooters to  feel  and  get  into  touch  with  each  other.
claims.description: Future battles will open with sharpshooters probing the enemy's outposts.

claims.quote: Cavalry  will  not  be  of  much  use  for  that  purpose.
claims.description: Cavalry will become of little use on the modern battlefield because mounted men are easy targets.

claims.quote: the  artillery  duel  will  commence  at  a range  of  from  four  to  five  miles.
claims.description: Long-range artillery duels at four to five miles will precede any infantry action.

claims.quote: But  the power  of  rifle-fire  is  so  great  that  it  will  be  absolutely impossible  for  the  combatants  to  get  to  close  quarters with  each  other.
claims.description: Massed rifle fire will make close-quarters combat impossible.

claims.quote: As  for  any  advance  in  force,  even  in the  loosest  of  formations,  on  a  front  that  is  swept  by  the enemies'  fire,  that  is  absolutely  out  of  the  question.
claims.description: Frontal infantry advances against a fire-swept front will be impossible.

claims.quote: Flank movements  may  be  attempted,  but  the  increased  power which  a  magazine  rifle  gives  to  the  defence  will  render it  impossible  for  such  movements  to  have  the  success that  they  formerly  had.
claims.description: Magazine rifles will give the defence such power that flanking movements will rarely succeed.

claims.quote: Certainly,  everybody  will  be  entrenched  in  the  next war.  It  will  be  a  great  war  of  entrenchments.
claims.description: The next great war will be fought by entrenched armies, a war of trenches.

claims.quote: The spade  will  be  as  indispensable  to  a  soldier  as  his  rifle.
claims.description: Every soldier will need to dig in; the entrenching spade becomes as essential as the rifle.

claims.quote: Battles  will  last  for  days,  and  at  the  end  it is  very  doubtful  whether  any  decisive  victory  can  be gained.
claims.description: Future battles will last for days and probably end without a decisive victory.

claims.quote: What seems  much  more  probable  is  that  with  the  excessive rapidity  of  fire,  armies  will  empty  their  magazines,  and the  army  that  fires  its  last  cartridge  first  will  be  at  the mercy  of  the  other.
claims.description: Rapid-fire weapons will exhaust armies' ammunition, leaving whichever runs out first at the enemy's mercy.

claims.quote: Then  the  old  veteran  Dragomiroff will  rejoice,  for  the  bayonet  will  once  more  come  into play.
claims.description: Once ammunition runs out, bayonet fighting will return.

claims.quote: Ammunition  will  not  give  out.
claims.description: Modern armies will not run short of ammunition.

claims.quote: Yet  with  all  this  movement  in  the  two  armies there  will  be  a  belt  a  thousand  paces  wide,  separating them  as  by  neutral  territory,  swept  by  the  fire  of  both sides,  a  belt  which  no  living  being  can  stand  for  a  moment.
claims.description: A fire-swept no man's land about a thousand paces wide will separate the opposing armies, and no one can cross it.

claims.quote: Melinite  bombs  will  turn  to  dust  farmhouses,  villages, and  hamlets,  destroying  everything  that  might  be  used  as cover,  obstacle,  or  refuge.
claims.description: High-explosive shells will level farms and villages across the battlefield.

claims.quote: The  moment  will  approach  when  half  the  combatants will  be  mowed  down,  dead  and  wounded  will  lie  in  parallel rows,
claims.description: Half of all combatants will be killed or wounded, lying in rows on either side of the fire zone.

claims.quote: Who  shall  have  gained  the  victory  ?     Neither.
claims.description: Battles in a future war will end with neither side victorious.

claims.quote: Such  are  constrained  to  admit  that  between  the  combatants will  always  be  an  impassable  zone  of  fire  deadly  in  an equal  degree  to  both  the  foes.
claims.description: Future wars will always have an impassable fire zone between the combatants.

claims.quote: It  is  much  more  probable  that  in  the  future  both  sides will  claim  the  victory.
claims.description: Future battles will be so indecisive that both sides will claim victory.

claims.quote: There  will  be  no  war  in  the  future,
claims.description: Great-power war has become impossible, since it would be suicide for the nations that wage it.

claims.quote: I  do  not  for  a  moment  deny  that  it  is  possible for  nations  to  plunge  themselves  and  their  neighbours into  a  frightful  series  of  catastrophes  which  would  probably result  in  the  overturn  of  all  civilised  and  ordered  government.
claims.description: A general war could still happen and would probably overthrow civilized government across Europe.

claims.quote: No  decisive  war  is  possible.
claims.description: No modern war can be decided by defeating the enemy on the battlefield.

claims.quote: Neither  is any  war  possible,  as  I  proceed  to  show,  that  will  not  entail, even  upon  the  victorious  Power,  the  destruction  of  its resources  and  the  break-up  of  society.
claims.description: Any modern war will ruin even the victor's resources and break up its society.

claims.quote: In  a  war  between  the  Triple and  the  Dual  Alliance  there  would  be  ten  millions  of  men under  arms.
claims.description: A war between the two European alliance blocs would mobilize about ten million men.

claims.quote: Hence  the  battle  will  be  spread  over  an  enormous  front, and  every  mile  over  which  you  spread  your  men  increases the  difficulties  of  supply,  of  mutual  co-operation,  and  of combined  effort.
claims.description: Battles will be spread across enormous fronts, straining supply and coordination.

claims.quote: the  war would  not  last  many  weeks  before  the  majority  of  the officers  had  been  killed  off.
claims.description: Most officers will be killed within the first weeks of a great war.

claims.quote: Hence,  under  modern  conditions  of  warfare  every  army will  tend  inevitably  to  degenerate  into  such  a  mob.
claims.description: Mass armies that lose their officers will degenerate into leaderless mobs.

claims.quote: The  largest possible  force  will  be  brought  to  the  front,  and  this  effort will  inevitably  result  in  the  breakdown  of  the  whole machine.
claims.description: Nations will mobilize the largest possible armies, and the effort will break down the whole military machine.

claims.quote: This  proportion  is  likely  to  be  much  increased  in future  wars.
claims.description: Invading armies will have to commit a much larger share of troops to guarding their communications.

claims.quote: Now  the  whole  line  of  communications will  be  exposed  to  dropping  shots  from  marksmen who,  from  the  security  of  thicket  or  hedge,  will  deal out  sudden  death  without  any  tell-tale  smoke
claims.description: Smokeless powder will let hidden snipers and guerrillas harass supply lines without being located.

claims.quote: The  first  thing  to  be  borne  in  mind  is  that  the next  war  will  be  a  long  war.
claims.description: The next great war will be long.

claims.quote: rendered  it  impossible  to  hope  that  any  decisive  result could  be  arrived  at  before  two  years  at  the  least.
claims.description: A great European war could not reach a decisive result in less than two years.
claims.stated_time: before two years at the least

claims.quote: In  reality  the  war  of  the  future,  if  ever  it takes  place,  will  not  be  fighting ;  it  will  be  terminated  by famine.
claims.description: A future war will be ended by famine and economic exhaustion rather than by fighting.

claims.quote: Because  all  wars  will  of  necessity  partake  of  the character  of  siege  operations.
claims.description: All future wars will take the form of siege warfare.

claims.quote: in  every  case  the  invading  army  would  find  itself confronted  by  lines  upon  lines  of  fortresses  and  fortified camps,  behind  which  would  stand  arrayed  forces  equal  or superior  in  number  to  those  which  it  could  bring  into  the field  against  them.
claims.description: Invaders will face continuous lines of fortresses and fortified camps along every frontier.

claims.quote: But  it  is  not  merely  that  each  fortress  would have  to  be  reduced,  but  every  field  would  more  or  less become  an  improvised  fortified  camp.
claims.description: Every field will become an improvised fortified position.

claims.quote: Long  and  harassing  siege  operations  in  a war  of  blockade  would  wear  out  the  patience  and  exhaust the  resources  of  armies.
claims.description: Prolonged siege and blockade warfare will exhaust armies' patience and resources.

claims.quote: The majority  of  the  population  tends  more  and  more  to gravitate  to  cities,  and  the  city  dweller  is  by  no  means  so capable  of  lying  out  at  nights  in  damp  and  exposed  positions as  the  peasant.
claims.description: Urbanization will produce soldiers less able to endure the hardships of a long campaign.

claims.quote: it  is  the  expectation  of  the  best  authorities that  they  would  have  100,000  men  in  hospital,  even if  never  a  shot  had  been  fired.
claims.description: Disease and exhaustion will put 100,000 soldiers in hospital within two weeks of mobilization.
claims.stated_time: In two weeks' time after the French army is mobilised

claims.quote: But  in  the  war  of  the  future  these humanities  will  go  the  wall.
claims.description: Ambulance and medical care for the wounded will break down in future war.
claims.stated_time: in the war of the future

claims.quote: The  consequence  is  they  will  be  left  to  lie where  they  fall,  and  they  may  lie  for  days.
claims.description: Wounded men will be left lying for days because stretcher-bearers cannot enter the fire zone.

claims.quote: What  is  much  more  likely  to  be  done  is  that  the  dying and  the  dead  will  be  utilised  as  ramparts  to  strengthen the   shelter   trenches.
claims.description: Bodies of the dead and dying will be used as ramparts in the trenches.

claims.quote: but  I  believe  that  war  will  be decided  not  by  these  things— not  even  by  fighting-men at  all,  but  by  the  factors  of  which  they  at  present  take  far too  little  account.
claims.description: Future war will be decided by economic and civilian factors rather than by soldiers.

claims.quote: That  element  in  the civil  population  will  be,  more  than  anything  else,  the deciding  factor  in  modern  war.
claims.description: The endurance of the civilian population on the home front will be the deciding factor in modern war.

claims.quote: The  men  at  the  front will  very  speedily  be  brought  to  a  deadlock.
claims.description: The fighting fronts will quickly reach a stalemate.

claims.quote: The  second factor,  which  perhaps  might  take  precedence  of  the  moral qualities,  is  whether  or  not  it  is  physically  possible  for the  population  left  behind  to  supply  the  armies  in  front with  what  they  need  to  carry  on  the  campaign.
claims.description: Victory will depend on whether the home economy can keep supplying the armies.
